title: What are they threatening?
summary: Turn the questions around. Before you move, look at the board from the other side.

steps.title: Look from the other side
steps.text:
Everything so far has been about what you can win. The same questions protect you when you ask them about your own pieces.

A **threat** is something your opponent could win if it were their move. The quick test: which of my pieces could they capture and come out ahead?

Good players do this before every move, as a routine, the way a pilot runs a checklist. It takes a few seconds and prevents most lost games.

steps.prompt: @W to move. Tap every @W piece that @B is threatening to win.
steps.explain: The pawn on @d5 attacks the knight, and the queen on @b6 attacks the loose bishop. Two threats, and one move can't meet both. Seeing threats before they arrive is how you avoid positions like this one.

steps.prompt: @W to move. Your knight on @d4 is attacked. Deal with it, and do better than just running away.

scaffold.prompt: Which @W piece is under threat? Tap it.

tempting.explain: N@c6 attacks two pawns and looks like a fork. But the bishop on @b5 simply takes the knight. A fork on a square the enemy controls is a gift.

reasons.question: Why is Nx@b5 the right answer?

choices.text: It moves the attacked knight and captures a loose bishop in the same move.
Any knight move is about as good. The bishop was not the point.
The knight on @d4 was never really in danger.

hints: What does the pawn on @e5 attack?
The knight has to move. Is there a square where it captures something?
steps.explain: Two questions, asked in order. What are they threatening? The knight. What is loose? The bishop. The move that answers both is the one to play.

steps.title: A routine before every move
steps.text:
Here is the routine this course will keep asking you to run. It is short on purpose.

1. **What did their last move threaten?** Look at what it attacks now.
2. **What is loose?** Theirs and yours.
3. **Checks, captures, threats.** List your forcing moves before your quiet ones.
4. **Blunder check.** After the move you want to play, what is loose, and what can they take?

You can turn on a reminder of this routine in Settings. It will appear above the board in puzzles until the habit is yours.
